# whatIf=true returns the completed-merge response without merging

**Claim.** A simulation answers exactly as a real merge does — same 200, same body, same Location pointing at the primary — while both records survive. The response is therefore no evidence that a merge happened.

Applies to: `~1people~1{vanId}~1mergeInto/put`

## Observed exchange

_Two records to merge: the primary would survive, the secondary would be consumed._

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Miles",
  "lastName": "Okafor-{scope}"
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```
```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Miles",
  "lastName": "Okafor-{scope}"
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000002
{
  "vanId": 100000002,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_Simulate with the literal string `true` — the only value that suppresses the write._

```http
PUT /people/100000002/mergeInto?whatIf=true

{
  "vanId": 100000001
}

→ 200
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001
}
```

_Nothing was written: the secondary is still there, unlike after a real merge._
